fps.title: FPS monitor: jank into measurable numbers
fps.hint1: Jank threshold: a frame over two frame budgets (~33ms) — where the eye notices stutter. The line tops at 60fps; dashed line is 30fps.
fps.hint2: Trade-off: summarize every 500ms before setState, not per frame. Otherwise the FPS component re-renders each frame and you measure the monitor’s overhead.

vscroll.title: Virtual scroll: render only visible rows
vscroll.hint1: Both lists use the same data. Scrollbar height is identical (

worker.title: Web Worker: move heavy computation off the main thread
worker.spinnerTitle: It freezes when the main thread is saturated
worker.hint: The top-right square is pure CSS, independent of JS. Click "Compute on main thread" and it freezes — the "freeze" users feel; click "Compute in Worker" and it keeps spinning while the UI stays interactive.
worker.noRecord: No measurements yet — click the two buttons above once each
worker.pitfall2: functions passed to createWorker are stringified and moved into the Worker, so they must be self-contained and cannot reference external closure variables (an inherent Worker limitation). Workers also have creation overhead, so only tasks that "feel laggy" are worth moving.

rerender.title: Re-render optimization: memo is not a cure-all
rerender.plainNote: it renders whenever the parent renders
rerender.looseNote: memo is useless here: a new reference every time
rerender.strictNote: skips rendering only when props truly stay the same
rerender.hint1: Click the buttons below and watch the three counters.
rerender.hintBold: ③ only moves when the "resource list" truly changes
rerender.hint2: — in every other case it skips rendering.
rerender.ctxHint1: Another common pitfall: Context changes pierce through
